requirements.title: Domain validation
requirements.text: The system shall validate that Domain values are in the range [0, 232] inclusive and return DomainOutOfRange for values outside this range.

requirements.title: Participant trait
requirements.text: The system shall expose a Participant trait with new_publisher, new_subscriber, domain, and close methods per RELAY spec §8.2.

requirements.title: new_publisher rejects empty topic
requirements.text: Participant::new_publisher shall return TopicEmpty when the topic argument is an empty string.

requirements.title: new_subscriber rejects empty topic
requirements.text: Participant::new_subscriber shall return TopicEmpty when the topic argument is an empty string.

requirements.title: Participant close is idempotent
requirements.text: Participant::close shall be idempotent; calling it more than once shall return Ok.

requirements.title: Operations after close return Closed
requirements.text: Calls to new_publisher and new_subscriber after Participant::close shall return Error::Closed.

requirements.title: Publisher trait
requirements.text: The system shall expose a Publisher trait with write, write_ctx, and close methods per RELAY spec §8.2.

requirements.title: write delivers to subscribers
requirements.text: Publisher::write shall deliver the payload to all active subscribers on the same topic.

requirements.title: write_ctx honours context deadline
requirements.text: Publisher::write_ctx shall return Error::Timeout when the context deadline has passed before the write completes.

requirements.title: Publisher close is idempotent
requirements.text: Publisher::close shall be idempotent; write after close shall return Error::Closed.

requirements.title: Subscriber trait
requirements.text: The system shall expose a Subscriber trait with unsubscribe and close methods per RELAY spec §8.2.

requirements.title: SampleReceiver
requirements.text: The system shall expose a SampleReceiver with async recv() and non-blocking try_recv() for consuming samples.

requirements.title: Sample fields
requirements.text: Sample shall carry topic, payload, timestamp, sequence_number, and writer_guid fields per RELAY spec §15.7.2.

requirements.title: Unsubscribe stops delivery
requirements.text: Subscriber::unsubscribe shall stop sample delivery without closing the SampleReceiver channel.

requirements.title: sequence_number is monotonic
requirements.text: Each publisher shall assign monotonically increasing sequence numbers to samples written on a topic.

requirements.title: ReliabilityKind
requirements.text: The system shall define BestEffort and Reliable reliability kinds per RELAY spec §8.2.

requirements.title: DurabilityKind
requirements.text: The system shall define Volatile and TransientLocal durability kinds per RELAY spec §8.2.

requirements.title: DefaultQoS
requirements.text: DEFAULT_QOS shall be BestEffort + Volatile with history depth 1.

requirements.title: ReliableQoS
requirements.text: RELIABLE_QOS shall be Reliable + TransientLocal with history depth 1.

requirements.title: TransientLocal cache
requirements.text: TransientLocal subscribers shall receive the last history_depth samples cached before they joined.

requirements.title: Back-pressure DropNewest
requirements.text: DropNewest policy shall drop the arriving sample when the subscriber channel is full.

requirements.title: Back-pressure DropOldest
requirements.text: DropOldest policy shall drop the oldest buffered sample to make room for the arriving sample.

requirements.title: Deadline QoS callback firing
requirements.text: When a subscriber's QoS.deadline_ns is non-zero and a Deadline-missed callback is registered, the system shall invoke that callback whenever deadline_ns nanoseconds elapse on that reader without a new sample being delivered, and shall continue to invoke it once per elapsed interval for as long as no sample arrives.

requirements.title: Deadline QoS timer reset
requirements.text: Each sample delivered to a subscriber with Deadline QoS enabled shall restart that reader's deadline window, so the Deadline-missed callback does not fire while samples keep arriving within the configured interval.

requirements.title: Mandatory sentinels
requirements.text: The system shall expose Closed, NotConnected, Timeout, and PayloadTooLarge error variants per RELAY spec §5.1.

requirements.title: DDS-specific errors
requirements.text: The system shall expose DDS-specific error variants including DomainOutOfRange, TopicEmpty, QosMismatch, DeadlineMissed, SampleRejected, ResourceLimits, LoanBuffer, and AccessDenied.

requirements.title: Error sentinel mapping
requirements.text: Error::as_relay() shall map each DDS-specific error to the nearest mandatory RELAY sentinel.

requirements.title: Sample to/from Message
requirements.text: Sample::to_message() and Sample::from_message() shall provide lossless round-trip conversion per RELAY spec §15.7.2.

requirements.title: RELAY Node adapter
requirements.text: adapt() shall wrap a Participant as a relay::Node routing send() to per-topic publishers and subscribe() to DDS subscribers.

requirements.title: subscribe requires topic
requirements.text: relay::Node::subscribe() shall return Error::NotConnected when SubscriberOptions has no topic set.

requirements.title: RELAY_SPEC_VERSION
requirements.text: The crate shall export RELAY_SPEC_VERSION = "1.11" per RELAY spec §19.4.

requirements.title: MockParticipant creation
requirements.text: MockParticipant::new shall validate the domain and return an in-process participant requiring no OS or network dependencies.

requirements.title: Mock broadcast
requirements.text: MockParticipant shall deliver samples written by a publisher to all active subscribers on the same topic.

requirements.title: Mock write log
requirements.text: MockParticipant shall record all written payloads accessible via written_payloads() and clearable via reset().

requirements.title: Concurrent safety
requirements.text: All trait implementations shall be safe to use from multiple async tasks concurrently (Send + Sync).

requirements.title: AtomicBool for closed flag
requirements.text: Participant and Publisher closed state shall be tracked with AtomicBool and checked before every operation.

requirements.title: Fault propagation (ISO 26262 ASIL-D)
requirements.text: All critical operations shall detect and propagate faults to the caller via the Error type; no silent failure or panic in safety-relevant code paths.

requirements.title: No unsafe code without justification (ISO 26262)
requirements.text: No unsafe Rust shall be used in any module without a documented safety argument justifying the absence of undefined behavior.

requirements.title: No panic in safety paths (ISO 26262)
requirements.text: No .unwrap() or .expect() shall appear in code reachable from safety-relevant API entry points; all Results shall be propagated.

requirements.title: Diagnostic coverage (ISO 26262 Part 5)
requirements.text: The system shall support diagnostic coverage measurement; every safety function shall be exercised by at least one test carrying a fusa:test annotation.

requirements.title: Sequence number overflow detection (ISO 26262)
requirements.text: Publisher sequence numbers shall be u64 monotonically increasing per-writer; the application shall detect rollover as a safety violation.

requirements.title: Input boundary validation (ISO 26262)
requirements.text: The Domain type shall reject values outside [0, 232] before any participant is created; boundary values 0 and 232 shall each be covered by an explicit test.

requirements.title: Deterministic state machine (ISO 26262)
requirements.text: Publisher and Participant state transitions (open → closed) shall be implemented with AtomicBool compare_exchange to prevent concurrent duplicate-close races.

requirements.title: Graceful allocation failure (ISO 26262)
requirements.text: Memory allocation failures in queue operations shall be handled via the back-pressure policy rather than panic; no unbounded allocation in write paths.

requirements.title: API contract documentation (ISO 26262)
requirements.text: All public APIs shall document their safety pre-conditions, post-conditions, and error returns in Rustdoc.

requirements.title: No busy-wait in safety paths (ISO 26262)
requirements.text: No thread::sleep or spin-loop shall be used in any path reachable during normal operation; blocking waits shall use async/await with tokio.

requirements.title: Testability without live dependency (IEC 61508 SIL-3)
requirements.text: All safety functions shall be testable in isolation using MockParticipant without any OS, network, or external process dependency.

requirements.title: Fail-safe on error (IEC 61508)
requirements.text: The system shall implement fail-safe behavior: on any detected error, return the error and halt further processing for that operation rather than attempting recovery that could mask the fault.

requirements.title: Bidirectional traceability (IEC 61508)
requirements.text: Every requirement in requirements.json shall have at least one fusa:req implementation annotation and at least one fusa:test test annotation, enabling bidirectional traceability.

requirements.title: Test completeness gate (IEC 61508)
requirements.text: CI shall enforce that every requirement ID appearing in requirements.json also appears in at least one fusa:test annotation in the test suite.

requirements.title: Output validity (IEC 61508)
requirements.text: The system shall not deliver samples to closed or unsubscribed channels; all output shall pass through the unsubscribed/closed guard before delivery.

requirements.title: Formal synchronization (IEC 61508)
requirements.text: All shared mutable state shall be protected by formal synchronization primitives (Mutex, AtomicBool); no unprotected shared state shall exist.

requirements.title: Drop counter on back-pressure (IEC 61508)
requirements.text: The system shall maintain visibility into dropped samples; future implementations shall expose drop counters accessible for diagnostic monitoring.

requirements.title: Deterministic safety functions (IEC 61508)
requirements.text: All safety functions shall be deterministic and free of external environmental dependencies; tests shall not rely on wall-clock timing except for explicit timeout tests.

requirements.title: Exhaustive error type (IEC 61508)
requirements.text: The Error enum shall be exhaustively matched in as_relay(); the wildcard arm (_) shall handle only variants with no RELAY sentinel mapping.

requirements.title: Atomic lifecycle enforcement (IEC 61508)
requirements.text: Participant and Publisher lifecycle transitions (open → closed) shall be enforced with AtomicBool::compare_exchange to guarantee at-most-once close semantics.

requirements.title: Bidirectional traceability (DO-178C DAL-A)
requirements.text: Every line of safety-relevant source code shall be traceable to at least one requirement via fusa:req, and every requirement shall be traceable to at least one test via fusa:test.

requirements.title: No dead code in safety modules (DO-178C)
requirements.text: No unreachable or dead code shall exist in participant.rs, error.rs, types.rs, or adapt.rs; CI lint shall fail on dead code warnings.

requirements.title: Decision coverage gate (DO-178C Modified Condition/Decision Coverage)
requirements.text: Every conditional branch in safety-relevant code shall be exercised by the test suite in both the true and false directions.

requirements.title: Documented assumptions (DO-178C)
requirements.text: All non-obvious constraints, assumed pre-conditions, and workarounds shall be documented with inline comments in the source.

requirements.title: Runtime version and conformance export (DO-178C)
requirements.text: The crate shall export RELAY_SPEC_VERSION and a capabilities function returning the protocol, version, and feature set at runtime.

requirements.title: Boundary condition tests (DO-178C)
requirements.text: Input boundary conditions (domain 0, domain 232, empty topic, max-depth queue) shall each have a dedicated test exercising the boundary value exactly.

requirements.title: Golden vector tests (DO-178C)
requirements.text: The Sample-to-Message conversion and back shall be verified by a golden-vector test using a known-good input/output pair with hardcoded expected bytes.

requirements.title: Concurrent path coverage (DO-178C)
requirements.text: Tests shall exercise concurrent publish and subscribe paths to detect data races; multi-subscriber broadcast and sequence number ordering shall be verified.

requirements.title: Topic name validation
requirements.text: The system shall reject topic names that are empty, exceed 256 bytes, or contain null bytes; TopicEmpty shall be returned for all such inputs.

requirements.title: Payload size limit
requirements.text: Publisher::write shall enforce a configurable maximum payload size; PayloadTooLarge shall be returned for payloads exceeding the limit.

requirements.title: Access denied error
requirements.text: The system shall expose an AccessDenied error variant to be returned when topic access is denied by an access control policy.

requirements.title: GUID deserialization validation
requirements.text: The dds.writer_guid field in relay::Message meta shall be validated on deserialization: it must be exactly 32 hex characters encoding 16 bytes.

requirements.title: No internal state in error messages
requirements.text: Error message strings shall not expose memory addresses, internal counters, or implementation details that could assist an attacker in information gathering.

requirements.title: Dependency CVE audit
requirements.text: CI shall run cargo audit on every push and pull request; a RUSTSEC advisory for any direct or transitive dependency shall be treated as a build-blocking failure.

requirements.title: Sequence number replay resistance
requirements.text: Monotonically increasing per-writer sequence numbers shall be included in every sample to support replay detection by the application layer.

requirements.title: Replay guard interface
requirements.text: The sequence_number field in Sample shall be exposed to applications so that replay-detection logic can compare against the last-seen sequence number per writer_guid.

requirements.title: Bounded queue allocation
requirements.text: Subscriber queues shall be bounded by the configured channel_depth; the Block back-pressure policy shall never allocate unbounded memory.

requirements.title: No secrets in message metadata
requirements.text: The relay::Message meta map shall not be used to transmit credentials, cryptographic keys, or any secret material; the spec does not define a confidentiality mechanism for meta.

requirements.title: Payload bounds enforcement
requirements.text: No buffer over-read shall occur during payload serialization or deserialization; all byte-slice operations shall use checked indexing or slice operations.

requirements.title: Bounded task spawning
requirements.text: The RELAY adapter shall not spawn unrestricted tasks; each subscribe() call spawns exactly one forwarding task, which terminates when the subscriber is closed.

requirements.title: Topic name character safety
requirements.text: Topic names shall be validated to contain only printable ASCII characters and forward slashes; null bytes and control characters shall cause TopicEmpty to be returned.

requirements.title: AccessDenied RELAY sentinel mapping
requirements.text: Error::AccessDenied shall map to relay::Error::NotConnected via as_relay() to prevent unauthorized access from appearing as a routing or transport failure.

requirements.title: No silent failures
requirements.text: All error conditions shall be surfaced via the Error return type; no safety- or security-relevant condition shall be silently swallowed.

requirements.title: No unaudited unsafe code
requirements.text: No unsafe block shall appear in any source file without a SAFETY comment documenting the invariant that makes it sound.

requirements.title: Bounded queue capacity
requirements.text: All subscriber queues shall be bounded to at most the configured channel_depth; the implementation shall not grow the queue beyond this limit.

requirements.title: Block policy capacity enforcement
requirements.text: The Block back-pressure policy shall be implemented as async backpressure that waits for space rather than growing the queue without bound.

requirements.title: Subscriber deallocation on close
requirements.text: The SubInner queue memory shall be released when the subscriber is closed; no subscriber allocation shall outlive its close() call.

requirements.title: No reference cycles
requirements.text: No Arc reference cycles shall exist in any data structure; all back-references shall use Weak or be avoided by design.

requirements.title: Bounded string allocation
requirements.text: All String values derived from external sources (topic names, meta values) shall be validated for maximum length before being stored.

requirements.title: O(1) push on hot path
requirements.text: SubInner::push shall complete in O(1) time under DropNewest and DropOldest policies; no iteration over the full queue shall occur during push.

requirements.title: Non-blocking try_recv
requirements.text: SampleReceiver::try_recv shall be non-blocking and return immediately with None when no sample is queued.

requirements.title: Close does not block on I/O
requirements.text: Participant::close in mock mode shall not block on any network I/O or external process; it shall complete synchronously after draining the subscriber list.

requirements.title: Bounded write latency
requirements.text: Publisher::write latency shall be bounded by queue capacity times message size under DropNewest or DropOldest; it shall not block indefinitely.

requirements.title: No dynamic allocation on hot path after init
requirements.text: After participant and publisher initialization, the write and deliver paths shall not perform dynamic memory allocation; all queues are pre-allocated to capacity.

requirements.title: relay-conform CI gate
requirements.text: CI MUST run `relay conform --strict` on the release binary and fail if any §12 schema validation returns FAIL or WARN (§20.1).

requirements.title: rsfusa CI gate
requirements.text: CI MUST run `rsfusa check` and fail if any ERROR-level finding is reported (§20.2).

requirements.title: MC/DC coverage objective (DO-178C DAL-A)
requirements.text: Every condition in every Boolean decision in safety-relevant code shall be independently exercised to affect the decision outcome; test cases shall demonstrate Modified Condition/Decision Coverage per DO-178C §6.4.4.2.

requirements.title: Test independence (DO-178C DAL-A)
requirements.text: Test cases shall be derived from requirements, not from implementation code; the author of tests shall have access only to the specification and not to the internal implementation details when designing test inputs and expected outputs.

requirements.title: Robustness and fault-injection testing (DO-178C)
requirements.text: The test suite shall include abnormal-input and boundary-violation tests for every external entry point: invalid domain values, empty topic strings, write after close, receive after unsubscribe, and expired context deadlines.

requirements.title: Software partitioning (DO-178C §2.5)
requirements.text: Modules shall be partitioned so that a failure in one module cannot corrupt data structures in another; internal state shall be accessible only through the module's defined interface.

requirements.title: Structural coverage reporting (DO-178C §6.4.4)
requirements.text: Statement and branch coverage shall be measured and reported for the test suite; CI shall record coverage metrics as a qualification evidence artefact.

requirements.title: No deactivated code (DO-178C §4.4.2)
requirements.text: No deactivated or dead code shall exist in safety-relevant modules; cargo clippy with dead_code deny and release-mode builds shall catch all such paths.

requirements.title: Coding standard enforcement (IEC 61508-3 §7.4.4)
requirements.text: A defined coding standard shall be enforced on every commit: cargo fmt for style and cargo clippy -D warnings for safety lints; deviations require documented justification.

requirements.title: Information hiding (IEC 61508-3 §7.4.3)
requirements.text: Internal mutable state (SubInner queue, Broker HashMap, AtomicBool flags) shall not be accessible outside their defining module; all access shall be through the public API.

requirements.title: Single-responsibility modular design (IEC 61508-3 §7.4.3)
requirements.text: Each source module shall have a single documented responsibility as defined in BOUNDARY.md §5; cross-module coupling shall be limited to the defined trait interfaces.

requirements.title: Defensive programming at external entry points (IEC 61508-3 §7.4.5)
requirements.text: Every function reachable from untrusted input (domain creation, publisher/subscriber creation, write) shall validate all inputs before proceeding; validation shall precede any state mutation.

requirements.title: Failure mode test coverage (IEC 61508-3 §7.9)
requirements.text: Every failure mode identified in fmea.json shall have at least one test that demonstrates the failure is detected and handled correctly; no FMEA entry shall be without a corresponding test.

requirements.title: Deadlock freedom
requirements.text: No code path shall acquire more than one mutex simultaneously; the single-lock protocol (one lock per SubInner push, one lock per Broker route, never nested) shall be maintained to guarantee deadlock freedom.

requirements.title: Starvation freedom under back-pressure
requirements.text: Under DropNewest or DropOldest back-pressure policies, a slow subscriber shall not prevent other subscribers or publishers from making progress; each SubInner has an independent queue and lock.

requirements.title: Deterministic meta ordering (BTreeMap)
requirements.text: relay::Message.meta shall use BTreeMap<String, String> to guarantee deterministic iteration order of metadata keys, independent of insertion order, per RELAY spec §18.3.

requirements.title: Sequence number strict monotonicity
requirements.text: The sequence_number in every Sample written by a single publisher shall be strictly greater than that of any previously written sample from the same publisher; the counter shall never decrease or reset during the publisher's lifetime.

requirements.title: Irreversible closed-state transition
requirements.text: Once a Participant or Publisher has been closed, the closed AtomicBool shall remain true; no operation shall transition the state back to open; subsequent close() calls shall succeed without side-effects.

requirements.title: DCO commit sign-off
requirements.text: Every commit merged to main shall carry a Developer Certificate of Origin Signed-off-by line; the DCO CI job shall block merges that violate this rule.

requirements.title: Semantic version release tagging
requirements.text: Every release of rust-DDS shall be tagged in the VCS with a semantic version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) corresponding to the version in Cargo.toml; no release shall be distributed without a corresponding VCS tag.

requirements.title: SBOM per release
requirements.text: A Software Bill of Materials (sbom.json) shall be generated and committed for every release, listing all direct and transitive dependencies with version and license information.

requirements.title: Back-pressure enforcement (HAZ-001, ASIL-B)
requirements.text: The configured back-pressure policy shall be applied on every write; under DropNewest, arriving samples that would exceed channel_depth shall be silently discarded; under DropOldest, the oldest enqueued sample shall be removed; under Block, the caller shall wait.

requirements.title: Payload integrity across transport (HAZ-002, ASIL-C)
requirements.text: A payload written by a publisher shall be delivered byte-for-byte identical to all active subscribers on the same topic; no modification, truncation, or corruption shall occur in the in-process mock transport.

requirements.title: Topic isolation — no cross-topic delivery (HAZ-003, ASIL-B)
requirements.text: A sample published on topic A shall never be delivered to a subscriber on topic B; the Broker routing table shall use exact string equality for topic matching.

requirements.title: Domain isolation — no cross-domain delivery (HAZ-004, ASIL-B)
requirements.text: A participant created on domain D shall not receive messages published by a participant on a different domain D'; each MockParticipant holds its own isolated Broker instance.

requirements.title: Unsubscribe closes recv channel (HAZ-005, ASIL-B)
requirements.text: After Subscriber::unsubscribe() is called, SampleReceiver::recv() shall return None rather than blocking indefinitely; the channel shall be closed by the unsubscribe call per RELAY spec §6.4.

requirements.title: Write-after-close returns Error::Closed (HAZ-007, ASIL-B)
requirements.text: Publisher::write or Publisher::write_ctx called after Publisher::close shall return Error::Closed and shall not deliver any payload to subscribers.

requirements.title: GuidPrefix/EntityId/GUID wire layout
requirements.text: The system shall encode a GuidPrefix as 12 raw bytes, an EntityId as 4 raw bytes, and a GUID as the 16-byte concatenation of GuidPrefix followed by EntityId, matching go-DDS's rtps.GUID layout (RTPS 2.3 §9.3.1) byte-for-byte.

requirements.title: Well-known EntityId constants
requirements.text: The system shall provide EntityId constants for Participant, SPDP writer/reader, and SEDP publication/subscription writer/reader matching the exact byte values of RTPS 2.3 Table 9.1 as implemented by go-DDS's rtps/guid.go.

requirements.title: Locator wire layout
requirements.text: The system shall encode a Locator as 24 little-endian bytes: 4-byte kind (i32) + 4-byte port (u32) + 16-byte address, matching go-DDS's rtps.marshalLocator (RTPS 2.3 §9.3.2) byte-for-byte.

requirements.title: ProtocolVersion wire layout
requirements.text: The system shall encode a ProtocolVersion as 2 raw bytes {major, minor} with no endian conversion, matching go-DDS's rtps.Header.ProtocolVersion field (RTPS 2.3 §9.3.2) byte-for-byte.

requirements.title: VendorId wire layout
requirements.text: The system shall encode a VendorId as 2 raw bytes with no endian conversion, matching go-DDS's rtps.Header.VendorId field (RTPS 2.3 §9.3.2) byte-for-byte, and shall define rust-DDS's own unregistered vendor ID distinct from go-DDS's 0x0127.

requirements.title: SequenceNumber wire layout
requirements.text: The system shall encode a SequenceNumber as 8 little-endian bytes: 4-byte high (i32) followed by 4-byte low (u32), matching go-DDS's rtps.SequenceNumber field layout (RTPS 2.3 §9.3.2) byte-for-byte.

requirements.title: SequenceNumber u64 packing without wraparound aliasing
requirements.text: The system shall provide to_u64/from_u64 conversions between SequenceNumber{high, low} and a single u64 that are bit-identical to go-DDS's snToU64/u64ToSN (rtps/reliable.go), so reliability bookkeeping never aliases after the low 32 bits wrap (RTPS 2.3 §8.3.5).

requirements.title: RTPS message Header wire layout
requirements.text: The system shall encode the fixed 20-byte RTPS message Header as the 4-byte magic "RTPS" followed by ProtocolVersion (2 bytes), VendorId (2 bytes), and GuidPrefix (12 bytes), matching go-DDS's rtps.marshalHeader (RTPS 2.3 §9.4.1) byte-for-byte, and shall reject decode input that does not start with the "RTPS" magic.

requirements.title: RTPS decode never panics on malformed input
requirements.text: Every decode function for RTPS wire types shall return a Result and never panic, index out of bounds, or unwrap on truncated or malformed input, since decoded bytes originate from an untrusted network transport.

requirements.title: SubmessageHeader wire layout
requirements.text: The system shall encode a SubmessageHeader as 4 bytes: 1-byte submessageId + 1-byte flags + 2-byte little-endian octetsToNextHeader, matching go-DDS's rtps submessage header layout (RTPS 2.3 §9.4.2) byte-for-byte, including the DATA/GAP/HEARTBEAT/ACKNACK/INFO_TS submessage ID constants and the Endianness/InlineQos/Data flag bits.

requirements.title: PL_CDR_LE parameter-list encoder header and parameter encoding
requirements.text: The system shall encode a PL_CDR_LE parameter list starting with a 4-byte encapsulation header (2-byte little-endian scheme 0x0003 + 2 zero option bytes) followed by zero or more parameters, each a 4-byte little-endian (PID, length) pair followed by the parameter value, matching go-DDS's rtps.plCDREncoder (RTPS 2.3 §10.2/§9.6.3) byte-for-byte.

requirements.title: CDR parameter value padding to a 4-byte boundary
requirements.text: The system shall pad every encoded parameter value up to the next multiple of 4 bytes with zero bytes and record the padded length (not the raw value length) in the parameter's length field, matching go-DDS's rtps.plCDREncoder.addParam byte-for-byte.

requirements.title: CDR string parameter encoding
requirements.text: The system shall encode a CDR string parameter as a 4-byte little-endian length (character count including a null terminator) followed by the UTF-8 bytes of the string and a single null terminator byte, before parameter padding is applied, matching go-DDS's rtps.plCDREncoder.addString byte-for-byte.

requirements.title: PL_CDR_LE parameter-list decoding
requirements.text: The system shall decode a PL_CDR_LE parameter list by iterating (PID, length, value) triples, skipping PID_PAD entries, terminating at PID_SENTINEL, and shall reject a payload whose first 4 bytes are not the PL_CDR_LE scheme, matching go-DDS's rtps.plCDRDecoder behaviourally.

requirements.title: CDR_LE/PL_CDR_LE payload encapsulation wrap/unwrap
requirements.text: The system shall prepend a 4-byte CDR_LE encapsulation header (scheme + zero options) to a raw payload, and shall strip a 4-byte encapsulation header accepting either the CDR_LE or PL_CDR_LE scheme, matching go-DDS's rtps.cdrWrapPayload/cdrUnwrapPayload byte-for-byte.

requirements.title: RTPS 2.3 §9.6.1 port-assignment formula
requirements.text: The system shall compute the SPDP metatraffic multicast port as 7400 + 250*domain, the metatraffic unicast port as 7400 + 250*domain + 10 + 2*participant_idx, and the user-data unicast port as 7400 + 250*domain + 11 + 2*participant_idx, matching go-DDS's rtps.metaMulticastPort/metaUnicastPort/userUnicastPort exactly.

requirements.title: SPDP discovery multicast group addresses
requirements.text: The system shall use 239.255.0.1 as the IPv4 SPDP discovery multicast group and FF03::1 as the IPv6 SPDP discovery multicast group, matching go-DDS's rtps.spdpMulticastAddr/spdpMulticastAddrV6.

requirements.title: UDP unicast socket bind with sequential port retry
requirements.text: The system shall bind an async UDP unicast socket (IPv4 on 0.0.0.0, IPv6 on [::], with IPv6 explicitly noted as having limited interop testing) on a requested port, and on bind failure shall retry sequentially on up to 16 subsequent ports before returning an error, matching go-DDS's rtps.newUnicastSocket/newUnicastSocketV6 retry behaviour.

requirements.title: Multicast receive socket with SO_REUSEADDR/SO_REUSEPORT
requirements.text: The system shall bind a UDP multicast receive socket with SO_REUSEADDR set (and SO_REUSEPORT where the platform supports it) so multiple local participants can share the same SPDP multicast port, and shall join the requested multicast group, using only the socket2 crate's safe API with no raw libc calls and no unsafe code (REQ-ASIL-002/REQ-MEM-001), matching go-DDS's net.ListenMulticastUDP sharing semantics.

requirements.title: Per-socket async receive loop dispatching via mpsc channel
requirements.text: The system shall spawn one tokio::task per UDP socket that loops UdpSocket::recv_from and pushes each received datagram (payload plus sender address) into an internal bounded mpsc channel, dropping the datagram if the channel is full and exiting the loop if the channel's receiver has been dropped, replacing go-DDS's single dataReceiveLoop goroutine that multiplexes all sockets.

requirements.title: DATA submessage encode/decode
requirements.text: The system shall encode a DATA submessage body as extraFlags(2, zero) + octetsToInlineQos(2, always 16) + readerId(4) + writerId(4) + seqNum(8) + serialised payload, and shall decode the same layout back into reader/writer EntityId, SequenceNumber, and an optional payload (present only when the D flag is set and body bytes remain), matching go-DDS's marshalDataSubmessage/parseDataSubmessage (RTPS 2.3 §9.4.5.3) byte-for-byte.

requirements.title: Submessage iteration over an RTPS message body
requirements.text: The system shall iterate the submessages in an RTPS message body by reading each 4-byte SubmessageHeader and advancing by its octetsToNextHeader length, stopping cleanly once fewer than 4 bytes remain and yielding a decode error (without panicking) if a declared length would run past the end of the input, matching go-DDS's parseSubmessages behaviourally.

requirements.title: RTPS message wrapping
requirements.text: The system shall prepend the 20-byte RTPS Header to already-encoded submessage bytes to form a complete RTPS message, matching go-DDS's wrapInRTPSMessage byte-for-byte.

requirements.title: Builtin endpoint availability bitmask
requirements.text: The system shall provide bit constants for the six SPDP/SEDP builtin endpoints (SPDP announcer/detector, SEDP publication announcer/detector, SEDP subscription announcer/detector) at the same bit positions as go-DDS's rtps/guid.go, such that advertising all six yields PID_BUILTIN_ENDPOINT_SET = 0x3f.

requirements.title: SPDP ParticipantProxy data encoding
requirements.text: The system shall encode an SPDP ParticipantProxy PL_CDR_LE payload containing, in order, the protocol version, vendor ID, participant GUID, builtin endpoint set, metatraffic unicast locator, default unicast locator, and participant lease duration, with the two unicast locators carrying an all-zero (0.0.0.0) address, matching go-DDS's buildParticipantData byte-for-byte.

requirements.title: SPDP ParticipantProxy data decoding with zero-address locator fill-in
requirements.text: The system shall decode an SPDP ParticipantProxy PL_CDR_LE payload field-by-field (tolerating missing parameters, which retain their default/zero value), and for any metatraffic or default unicast locator whose address is all-zero shall fill in the IPv4 address of the announcement's UDP sender, matching go-DDS's parseParticipantData behaviourally; malformed input (an invalid PL_CDR_LE header) shall yield no result rather than panicking.

requirements.title: SPDP periodic multicast announcement with jitter
requirements.text: The system shall send an SPDP announcement to the domain's SPDP multicast group immediately on startup and then at a configurable periodic interval (default 2 seconds), optionally preceded by a uniformly-random delay bounded by a configurable jitter duration before each periodic (not the initial) announcement, matching go-DDS's spdpService.announceLoop behaviourally.

requirements.title: SPDP known-participants table with lease-based eviction and self-filtering
requirements.text: The system shall maintain a table of known remote participants keyed by GUID prefix, updating each entry's last-seen time on every valid SPDP announcement received (applying a default 10-second lease when the peer's announcement did not carry one), shall periodically (once per second) evict any peer whose lease has expired, and shall ignore SPDP announcements whose GUID prefix matches the local participant's own, matching go-DDS's spdpService.storePeer/evictLoop/handlePacket behaviourally.

requirements.title: SEDP EndpointData PL_CDR_LE encoding
requirements.text: The system shall encode a SEDP publication/subscription EndpointData payload as a PL_CDR_LE parameter list containing the endpoint's GUID, its topic name, a hard-coded 'CDR_BLOB' type name, and a default unicast locator whose address is all-zero (filled in by the receiver from the announcement's UDP sender address), matching go-DDS's buildEndpointData byte-for-byte.

requirements.title: SEDP EndpointData decoding with zero-address locator fill-in
requirements.text: The system shall decode a SEDP EndpointData PL_CDR_LE payload field-by-field, filling in the IPv4 address of an all-zero default unicast locator from the announcement's UDP sender address, and shall discard the announcement without storing it if it carries no topic name, matching go-DDS's handleEndpointAnnounce behaviourally; malformed input (an invalid PL_CDR_LE header) shall be ignored rather than causing a panic.

requirements.title: SEDP local endpoint registration and announcement
requirements.text: The system shall record each locally registered writer or reader, immediately broadcast a SEDP publication or subscription announcement for it to every participant known to SpdpService, and shall announce every already-registered local endpoint to a single newly-discovered peer on request, matching go-DDS's registerWriter/registerReader/onNewPeer behaviourally.

requirements.title: SEDP remote endpoint topic matching
requirements.text: The system shall match a newly-discovered remote writer against every local reader sharing its topic name (recording the remote data-delivery locator for each match), shall match a newly-registered local reader against every already-discovered remote writer sharing its topic name, and shall record every discovered remote reader with its data-delivery locator so that matched-reader-locator queries return exactly the peers subscribed to a given topic, matching go-DDS's onRemoteWriter/onRemoteReader/registerReader behaviourally.

requirements.title: SEDP peer eviction propagation
requirements.text: The system shall remove every remote writer, remote reader, remote reader locator, and matched writer locator associated with a given GUID prefix when that participant is evicted, matching go-DDS's onPeerEvicted behaviourally.

requirements.title: SEDP receive-loop packet dispatch with self-filtering
requirements.text: The system shall decode each received datagram as an RTPS message, ignore it if its GUID prefix matches the local participant, and dispatch each DATA submessage whose writer entity ID is the SEDP publications or subscriptions writer to endpoint-announcement handling; malformed input, non-DATA submessages, and DATA submessages from neither SEDP writer entity shall be silently ignored rather than causing a panic, matching go-DDS's handlePacket/receiveLoop behaviourally.

requirements.title: Locator-to-SocketAddr conversion for RTPS unicast send
requirements.text: The system shall convert a UDPv4 or UDPv6 Locator to a SocketAddr usable as a UDP send destination, and shall return no result rather than panicking for a locator of any other kind or a port value that does not fit in 16 bits, matching go-DDS's Locator.udpAddr behaviourally.

requirements.title: User-defined entity ID assignment
requirements.text: The system shall derive a user-defined writer or reader EntityId from a per-participant strictly-increasing counter, packing the counter's low 24 bits into the first three octets and a fixed entity-kind octet (0x03 for a writer, 0x04 for a reader) into the fourth, matching go-DDS's entityIdForWriter/entityIdForReader byte-for-byte.

requirements.title: BestEffort DATA submessage composition on write
requirements.text: The system shall, on each local write, assign the next per-writer sequence number, wrap the payload in a CDR_LE encapsulation header, encode a DATA submessage carrying it (with no inline QoS and no history retained), and wrap the result in an RTPS message, matching go-DDS's rtpsWriter.Write's BestEffort (non-reliable) path byte-for-byte for the composition of already-verified primitives.

requirements.title: Sample dispatch to matched local readers by topic and writer GUID
requirements.text: The system shall deliver a written or received sample to every local reader whose topic matches (when a topic filter is supplied) and which accepts the sample's source writer GUID, where a reader with no SEDP-matched sources accepts only writers sharing its own participant's GUID prefix, and a reader with at least one SEDP-matched source additionally accepts any explicitly-matched remote writer GUID, matching go-DDS's dispatchToReaders/rtpsReader.acceptsSource behaviourally.

requirements.title: Asynchronous SEDP writer-match propagation to registered readers
requirements.text: The system shall notify a listener when SEDP's receive loop matches a newly-discovered remote writer against an already-registered local reader's topic, and the participant runtime shall add that writer's GUID to the reader's accepted-source set on receipt, matching go-DDS's onRemoteWriter calling rtpsReader.addSourceGUID in-line.

requirements.title: Inbound DATA submessage decode and dispatch
requirements.text: The system shall decode each received datagram as an RTPS message, ignore it if its GUID prefix matches the local participant, and for each DATA submessage unwrap its CDR payload and dispatch it to matched local readers keyed by writer GUID; malformed input and non-DATA submessages shall be silently ignored rather than causing a panic, matching go-DDS's handleDataPacket's BestEffort path behaviourally.

requirements.title: RTPS participant runtime writer/reader registration
requirements.text: The system shall assign a fresh entity ID and register a new local writer or reader with SEDP on creation, shall return a sample-receiving handle sharing the same queue/back-pressure type as the crate's in-process mock transport, and shall remove a reader from the dispatch table on unsubscribe, matching go-DDS's NewPublisher/NewSubscriber/rtpsReader.Unsubscribe registration bookkeeping.

requirements.title: SPDP peer-discovery bridge into SEDP
requirements.text: The system shall notify a listener with a copy of every ParticipantProxy SPDP stores from a decoded announcement, including repeat announcements from an already-known peer, and the participant runtime shall forward each into SEDP's new-peer announcement handling, matching go-DDS's spdpService.handlePacket calling sedpService.onNewPeer directly on every successfully decoded announcement.

requirements.title: HEARTBEAT submessage codec
requirements.text: The system shall encode and decode a HEARTBEAT submessage (reader/writer entity IDs, first and last sequence number, monotonically increasing count) as a 4-byte submessage header plus a 28-byte body, matching go-DDS's marshalHeartbeat/parseHeartbeat byte-for-byte; decode shall never panic on truncated input.

requirements.title: ACKNACK submessage codec
requirements.text: The system shall encode and decode an ACKNACK submessage (reader/writer entity IDs, base sequence number, a fixed 32-bit missing-sequence-number bitmap, monotonically increasing count) as a 4-byte submessage header plus a 28-byte body, matching go-DDS's marshalAckNack/parseAckNack byte-for-byte; decode shall never panic on truncated input.

requirements.title: GAP submessage codec
requirements.text: The system shall encode a GAP submessage declaring a contiguous inclusive range of permanently-unavailable sequence numbers as a 4-byte submessage header plus a 28-byte body (gapList bitmapBase = gapEnd.low + 1, numBits = 0), matching go-DDS's marshalGAP byte-for-byte.

requirements.title: Per-writer send-history retention
requirements.text: The system shall retain, per reliable writer, the last 256 sent RTPS wire messages in a fixed-size ring buffer keyed by full 64-bit sequence number, retrievable by sequence number while retained and reporting the lowest/highest retained sequence number, matching go-DDS's sendHistory (store/get/firstLast) behaviourally.

requirements.title: Per-remote-writer receive gap tracking
requirements.text: The system shall track, per reliable reader per remote writer, a cumulative-ACK watermark that advances only over a contiguous run of received sequence numbers, buffering out-of-order arrivals, and shall compute the ACKNACK base and 32-bit missing-sequence-number bitmap for a given upper bound, matching go-DDS's recvTracker (initExpected/record/missing) behaviourally.

requirements.title: Bounded out-of-order buffering
requirements.text: The system shall bound the receive-side gap tracker's out-of-order buffer to sequence numbers within 8192 of the current watermark, so a misbehaving or malicious writer cannot cause unbounded memory growth, matching go-DDS's maxReorderAhead.

requirements.title: Heartbeat period constant
requirements.text: The system shall use a 200-millisecond period for a reliable writer's periodic HEARTBEAT ticker, matching go-DDS's heartbeatPeriod constant.

requirements.title: Reliable writer/reader runtime wiring
requirements.text: The system shall, for a reliable writer, store every written sample in its send history and send a HEARTBEAT immediately after each write and periodically thereafter; shall, on receipt of a DATA or HEARTBEAT submessage, update every accepting reliable reader's gap tracker and send an ACKNACK back to the sender when a gap is detected; and shall, on receipt of an ACKNACK, advance the writer's acknowledged watermark, retransmit each still-retained requested sample to every matched reader locator, and send a GAP for any requested range already evicted from history, matching go-DDS's rtpsWriter.sendHeartbeatLocked/notifyReliableReaders/handleHeartbeat/handleAckNack/advanceAcked behaviourally.

requirements.title: Reliable reader registration
requirements.text: The system shall register a new local reliable reader the same way as a BestEffort reader (entity-id assignment, SEDP registration, matched-source pre-population) plus a lazily-populated per-remote-writer gap-tracker table, matching go-DDS's NewSubscriber registration for a reliable rtpsReader.

requirements.title: DATA_FRAG submessage codec
requirements.text: The system shall encode and decode a DATA_FRAG submessage (extraFlags, octetsToInlineQos, reader/writer EntityId, writer SequenceNumber, fragmentStartingNum, fragmentsInSubmsg, fragmentSize, dataSize, and fragment payload bytes) byte-for-byte matching go-DDS's marshalDataFrag/parseDataFrag, and shall never panic on truncated or malformed input.

requirements.title: DATA_FRAG reassembly
requirements.text: The system shall reassemble DATA_FRAG submessages for a given writer and sequence number into the original payload once every fragment has arrived, tolerating out-of-order and duplicate fragment delivery; shall reject a claimed DataSize above a fixed cap before allocating any reassembly buffer; shall evict an incomplete reassembly older than a fixed staleness age; and shall never panic on a fragment whose declared layout is inconsistent with its carried payload length, matching go-DDS's fragmentAssembler behaviourally while adding this no-panic guard for a live (untrusted-input) receive path.

requirements.title: Sender-side fragment splitting
requirements.text: The system shall split a payload larger than a configured per-fragment size into a sequence of DATA_FRAG fragments, each carrying a 1-based FragmentStartingNum, a single fragment per submessage, and the total unfragmented DataSize, matching go-DDS's splitIntoFragments/splitIntoFragmentsN byte-for-byte, including falling back to the default fragment size when given a zero size.

requirements.title: Writer/participant fragmentation wiring
requirements.text: The system shall, for a writer whose CDR-wrapped payload exceeds the default per-fragment size, send DATA_FRAG submessages instead of a single DATA submessage, matching go-DDS's rtpsWriter.Write; and shall, on receipt of a DATA_FRAG submessage, feed it to a per-participant fragment reassembly buffer and dispatch the completed reassembly to matched local readers exactly like a completed DATA submessage, including reliable-reader gap tracking and reactive ACKNACK.

requirements.title: Topic wildcard matching
requirements.text: The system shall report whether an MQTT-style topic pattern (where '+' matches exactly one topic level and '#' at the end of a segment matches zero or more remaining levels) matches a concrete topic name, matching go-DDS's TopicMatches behaviourally for the same pattern/topic pairs; and the participant's local-reader dispatch path shall use this matching as a fallback when a reader's registered topic is not a literal match for a writer's topic, matching go-DDS's dispatchToReaders' use of TopicMatches exactly (and nowhere else, matching go-DDS's own SEDP endpoint-matching code, which never calls TopicMatches).

requirements.title: TransientLocal durability persistence
requirements.text: The system shall, when configured with a persistence directory, persist the most recently written payload for each topic to a single file per topic (a 4-byte little-endian length prefix followed by the raw payload bytes) on every write, and shall load a topic's persisted payload from disk to deliver to a newly-registered TransientLocal reader when no in-memory last sample exists yet for that topic, matching go-DDS's WithPersistentHistory/persistLoad/persistFlush behaviourally and byte-for-byte for the on-disk file format; disk I/O failures during load or flush shall never panic or propagate as a write failure to the caller.

requirements.title: pcap-fixture wire-format conformance
requirements.text: The system shall provide a pure encoder and decoder for the standard libpcap file format (global header plus per-record IPv4/UDP framing) sufficient to read a checked-in fixture of known-good RTPS 2.3 section-9 messages sourced from go-DDS's real encoder, and decoding each recorded message's RTPS Header and submessage stream shall reproduce the exact same field values and bytes as go-DDS's own reference output for those messages, so that wire-format regressions in this crate's RTPS decode path are caught without requiring a live peer process; decoding malformed or truncated pcap input shall never panic.

requirements.title: SPDP static unicast peer discovery
requirements.text: The system shall allow a participant's SPDP configuration to carry a list of static peer unicast addresses and, independently, a flag disabling the SPDP multicast send; when sending an SPDP announcement, the system shall send the same ParticipantData payload directly (unicast) to every configured peer address, in addition to the multicast group unless multicast is disabled, in which case only the configured peer addresses are sent to; the ParticipantData payload and RTPS message framing shall be unchanged from the multicast case (no new wire format), and an incoming SPDP announcement shall be processed identically regardless of whether it arrived via a multicast-joined socket or a unicast one.

requirements.title: User-data multicast group and port formula
requirements.text: The system shall define the RTPS 2.3 §9.6.1 user-data multicast group IPv4 address (239.255.0.2) and a domain-scoped user-data multicast port formula (port_base + domain_gain*domain + 1, one port shared by every participant on the domain, no per-participant term), matching go-DDS's userDataMulticastAddr/userMulticastPort exactly.

requirements.title: BestEffort writer multicast delivery
requirements.text: The system shall allow a participant's user-data multicast send destination to be configured independently of construction, and a writer's write shall, when that destination is configured and at least one remote reader is currently SEDP-matched to the writer's topic, send each wire message exactly once to the configured multicast destination instead of once per matched reader's unicast locator; when no multicast destination is configured, or no remote reader is currently matched, the writer's existing per-locator unicast send path shall be used unchanged, matching go-DDS's rtpsWriter.Write dataMcastSock behaviour.

requirements.title: User-data multicast receive wiring and config gating
requirements.text: The system's public UDP-backed participant shall, unless configured with multicast disabled, attempt to bind and join the user-data multicast group at construction, treating a bind failure as non-fatal (falling back to unicast-only delivery, never propagated as a construction error); when the bind succeeds, the system shall configure this participant's writers to send to that multicast group and shall feed every datagram received on that socket into the same dispatch path used for the unicast data socket, so a matched local reader receives a multicast-delivered sample identically to a unicast-delivered one; the same configuration flag that disables SPDP discovery multicast shall also disable user-data multicast, so a single flag covers both multicast sockets a participant ever binds.

requirements.title: General-purpose XCDR1 primitive encode/decode
requirements.text: The system shall provide a general-purpose CDR/XCDR1 encoder and decoder for typed, non-opaque RTPS payloads (distinct from the PL_CDR_LE parameter-list codec) supporting bool, octet (signed and unsigned), char, 16/32/64-bit signed and unsigned integers, and 32/64-bit IEEE 754 floats, little-endian, each aligned to its own size (1 byte for bool/octet/char, 2 for 16-bit, 4 for 32-bit, 8 for 64-bit) counted from the start of the encoded buffer including its 4-byte CDR_LE encapsulation header, matching go-DDS's tools/cdr package (cdr.Encoder/cdr.Decoder primitive Write*/Read* methods) byte-for-byte.

requirements.title: General-purpose XCDR1 string and byte-sequence encode
requirements.text: The system shall encode a CDR string as a 4-byte little-endian length (character count including a null terminator, 4-byte aligned) followed by the UTF-8 bytes and a null terminator, and shall encode a byte sequence as a 4-byte little-endian element count (4-byte aligned) followed by the raw bytes with no per-element padding, matching go-DDS's tools/cdr package (cdr.Encoder.WriteString/WriteBytes) byte-for-byte; sequences of other primitive or composite types are composed by callers from a leading element-count write followed by that many per-element writes, the same convention go-DDS's cdr package itself uses (no dedicated typed-sequence method beyond WriteBytes).

requirements.title: General-purpose XCDR1 primitive decode error handling
requirements.text: The system's general-purpose XCDR1 decoder shall reject a buffer shorter than the 4-byte CDR encapsulation header or whose header scheme is neither CDR_LE (0x0001) nor CDR_BE (0x0000, accepted on the header without a big-endian decode path, matching go-DDS's own decoder behaviour), and every primitive read shall return an error rather than panic or index out of bounds when fewer bytes remain than the field requires at the current (alignment-adjusted) cursor position, matching go-DDS's tools/cdr package (cdr.Decoder primitive Read* methods and its need()/NewDecoder error paths) behaviourally.

requirements.title: General-purpose XCDR1 string and byte-sequence decode error handling
requirements.text: The system's general-purpose XCDR1 decoder shall decode a CDR string/byte-sequence by reading its 4-byte length/count prefix and then that many bytes, returning an error rather than panicking or indexing out of bounds when the declared length exceeds the remaining buffer, and shall lossily convert invalid UTF-8 in a decoded string rather than rejecting it outright so malformed or hostile input cannot abort decoding of the rest of the message, matching go-DDS's tools/cdr package (cdr.Decoder.ReadString/ReadBytes) behaviourally with that one deliberate safety deviation (go-DDS's ReadString does not validate UTF-8 at all, since Go strings may hold arbitrary bytes).

requirements.title: ShmemParticipant construction and domain validation
requirements.text: The system shall provide a shmem::ShmemParticipant implementing the Participant/Publisher/Subscriber traits, constructed via ShmemParticipant::new(domain), validating domain into the same [0, 232] range as every other Participant implementation and returning Error::DomainOutOfRange outside it; ShmemParticipant::close shall be idempotent and, after close, new_publisher shall return Error::Closed.

requirements.title: Same-process delivery via a shared in-process broker
requirements.text: Every ShmemParticipant constructed for the same Domain within one OS process shall share one in-process broker, and Publisher::write on a topic shall deliver the sample exactly once to every current process-local Subscriber registered on that same topic, with zero file I/O on the delivery path to those subscribers.

requirements.title: Cross-process delivery via a per-topic rendezvous file
requirements.text: Publisher::write shall additionally write the sample to a per-(domain, topic) rendezvous file on disk, atomically (write-then-rename) so a concurrent reader never observes a torn write; a Subscriber in a different OS process on the same domain and topic shall receive the sample by polling that file, with the writing process's own same-process subscribers not redelivered the same sample a second time through the cross-process path.

requirements.title: TransientLocal late-joiner delivery, in-process and cross-process
requirements.text: A Subscriber created with QoS::durability == TransientLocal shall receive the topic's last published value: from the in-process broker's cache when the last writer was in the same OS process, or from the current content of the cross-process rendezvous file when the last writer was a different OS process (including one that has already exited); a Subscriber created with QoS::durability == Volatile shall never receive a sample published before it was created, on either path.

requirements.title: MaxSampleSize enforced on shmem writes
requirements.text: shmem::ShmemPublisher::write shall return Error::PayloadTooLarge when QoS::max_sample_size is non-zero and the payload exceeds it, and shall accept any payload size when QoS::max_sample_size is zero, matching mock::MockParticipant's enforcement.

requirements.title: Domain isolation for the shmem transport
requirements.text: Participants on different Domain values shall never share an in-process broker and shall never share a cross-process rendezvous file, even when constructed with an identical topic name; a sample published on one domain shall never be delivered to a subscriber on a different domain via either the in-process or cross-process path.

requirements.title: Topic isolation for the shmem transport
requirements.text: A sample published on one topic shall never be delivered to a subscriber registered on a different topic, on either the in-process broker path or the cross-process rendezvous-file path.

requirements.title: Publisher/Subscriber lifecycle on the shmem transport
requirements.text: shmem::ShmemPublisher::write shall return Error::Closed after Publisher::close; shmem::ShmemParticipant::close shall be idempotent and, once closed, new_publisher and new_subscriber shall return Error::Closed; Subscriber::close shall stop both the in-process and cross-process delivery paths for that subscriber and cause SampleReceiver::recv to return None once drained.

requirements.title: LoaningPublisher trait extends Publisher
requirements.text: The system shall expose a LoaningPublisher trait extending Publisher with loan(size) and commit(buf) methods, and shmem::ShmemParticipant shall provide a constructor returning a LoaningPublisher backed by the shmem transport; loan shall return Error::Closed once the underlying publisher is closed.

requirements.title: Loan returns a pool-backed pre-allocated buffer
requirements.text: LoaningPublisher::loan(size) shall return a buffer of length size backed by the publisher's internal buffer pool rather than a fresh heap allocation whenever the pool has a suitably-sized buffer available, and shall return Error::LoanBuffer when size exceeds the pool's configured minimum capacity.

requirements.title: Commit publishes the loaned buffer and returns it to the pool
requirements.text: LoaningPublisher::commit(buf) shall publish buf via the same delivery path as Publisher::write and shall return buf to the pool for reuse by a subsequent loan call regardless of whether the publish succeeded.

requirements.title: SecurityPlugin seal/open contract
requirements.text: The system shall define a SecurityPlugin trait with seal(&self, plaintext: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, SecurityError> and open(&self, ciphertext: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, SecurityError> methods, such that for any conforming implementation and any plaintext, open(seal(plaintext)?)? == plaintext; open shall return Err, never panic, for input not produced by the matching seal call.

requirements.title: SecurityPlugin object safety
requirements.text: SecurityPlugin shall be object-safe (dyn-compatible) so that a security plugin can be selected and stored at runtime as Box<dyn SecurityPlugin> or Arc<dyn SecurityPlugin> without the caller knowing the concrete plugin type at compile time.

requirements.title: SecurityPlugin concurrency safety
requirements.text: Every SecurityPlugin implementation shall be Send + Sync, so that a single plugin instance can be shared (e.g. behind an Arc) across concurrent tokio tasks without additional synchronization by the caller.

requirements.title: NullPlugin identity transform
requirements.text: The system shall provide a NullPlugin implementation of SecurityPlugin whose seal and open methods return the input unchanged and never fail, for use when no payload security is required (development, testing, or interop with a non-secured peer), matching go-DDS's NullPlugin behaviourally.

requirements.title: HmacPlugin tag append
requirements.text: The system shall provide an HmacPlugin implementation of SecurityPlugin whose seal() appends a 32-byte HMAC-SHA-256 tag (computed under the plugin's key over the plaintext) to the end of the plaintext, and whose open() verifies that tag and returns the plaintext with the tag stripped, matching go-DDS's HMACPlugin (security/security.go) wire format and behaviour byte-for-byte.

requirements.title: HmacPlugin verification failure handling
requirements.text: HmacPlugin::open shall return SecurityError::PayloadTooShort if the input is shorter than the 32-byte HMAC tag, and SecurityError::VerificationFailed if the tag does not verify (including tampered plaintext, tampered tag, truncated ciphertext, or a mismatched key) using a constant-time tag comparison; open shall never panic and shall never return plaintext bytes when verification fails.

requirements.title: AesGcmPlugin encryption and framing
requirements.text: The system shall provide an AesGcmPlugin implementation of SecurityPlugin whose seal() requires an exactly 32-byte key (returning SecurityError::Other for any other length) and encrypts the plaintext with AES-256-GCM under a fresh, independently random 12-byte nonce for every call, returning nonce || ciphertext || GCM-tag[16], matching go-DDS's AESGCMPlugin (security/security.go) wire format and behaviour byte-for-byte.

requirements.title: AesGcmPlugin verification failure handling
requirements.text: AesGcmPlugin::open shall return SecurityError::PayloadTooShort if the input is shorter than 28 bytes (12-byte nonce plus 16-byte GCM tag), and SecurityError::VerificationFailed if authenticated decryption fails (including a tampered nonce, tampered ciphertext, tampered tag, truncated ciphertext, or a mismatched key); open shall never panic and shall never return plaintext bytes when verification fails.

requirements.title: AccessPolicy topic permission evaluation
requirements.text: The system shall provide an AccessPolicy type constructed from an ordered list of Rule (topic glob pattern, Permission) pairs whose can_read()/can_write() evaluate rules in declaration order and return true only if the first rule whose pattern matches the topic name (using Go stdlib path.Match shell-glob semantics: '*' matches a non-'/' run, '?' matches one non-'/' byte, '[...]' is a character class, '\\' escapes) grants the corresponding Permission::READ/WRITE bit, matching go-DDS's AccessPolicy (security/access.go) byte-for-byte, including its glob-matching algorithm.

requirements.title: AccessPolicy default-deny and malformed-pattern handling
requirements.text: AccessPolicy::can_read/can_write shall return false (deny) for a topic that matches no rule, shall stop evaluating further rules once an earlier rule in declaration order matches (first-match-wins, even if that rule denies the permission being checked), and shall silently skip any rule whose pattern is malformed (e.g. unterminated or empty character class) rather than treating it as a match or surfacing an error; evaluation shall never panic on any topic name or pattern input.

requirements.title: ReplayGuard sliding-window replay detection
requirements.text: The system shall provide a ReplayGuard type constructed with a sliding time window (a zero window substituted with a 30-second default) whose check(seq, ts) records seq (keyed on ts) and returns Ok(()) the first time seq is seen within window of ts, and returns ReplayError without re-recording the timestamp on every subsequent call for the same seq within that window, matching go-DDS's ReplayGuard (security/replay.go) behaviour.

requirements.title: ReplayGuard window pruning and concurrency safety
requirements.text: ReplayGuard::check shall prune, on every call, all recorded entries whose timestamp is more than window before the call's ts, allowing a previously-seen sequence number to be accepted again once it falls outside the window; ReplayGuard::purge shall perform the same pruning against the current time on demand; ReplayGuard::len shall report the number of currently-tracked entries; and ReplayGuard shall be Send + Sync and safe for concurrent use from multiple tokio tasks without the caller adding external synchronization, matching go-DDS's ReplayGuard.Purge/Len and its documented safe-for-concurrent-use contract.

requirements.title: HMAC-SHA-256 SPDP discovery authentication — signing
requirements.text: The system shall provide a DiscoveryPlugin trait and an HmacDiscoveryPlugin implementation whose sign_discovery(guid_prefix) returns a 32-byte HMAC-SHA-256 tag computed over a fixed context string followed by guid_prefix, matching go-DDS's HMACDiscoveryPlugin.SignDiscovery (security/discovery.go) byte-for-byte; when an SpdpConfig::discovery_plugin is configured, build_participant_data shall embed that tag in outbound SPDP announcements as a PID_DISCOVERY_TOKEN PL_CDR_LE parameter, matching go-DDS's spdpService.buildParticipantData wiring, and shall omit it entirely when no plugin is configured.

requirements.title: HMAC-SHA-256 SPDP discovery authentication — verification and rejection
requirements.text: HmacDiscoveryPlugin::verify_discovery shall return false for a nil/empty tag and otherwise recompute and compare the expected tag in constant time, returning true only for a tag produced by sign_discovery under the same key and guid_prefix; when SpdpService's configured discovery_plugin rejects a received announcement's PID_DISCOVERY_TOKEN (or the token is absent) against the sending participant's GuidPrefix, handle_packet shall silently discard that announcement without storing it as a known peer or notifying SEDP, matching go-DDS's spdpService.handlePacket verification gate; this check shall never panic on malformed or missing token input.

requirements.title: HealthStatus and Health value types
requirements.text: The system shall provide a HealthStatus enum with exactly three variants (Ok, Degraded, Down, defaulting to Ok) and a Health struct pairing a HealthStatus with an optional details string, matching go-DDS's dds.HealthStatus/dds.Health (dds.go); HealthStatus's Display implementation and its serde representation shall both render the lowercase strings "ok"/"degraded"/"down", matching go-DDS's HealthStatus.String() byte-for-byte, and Health shall omit its details field when serialized to JSON if no details are present, matching go-DDS's `json:"details,omitempty"` behaviour for an empty string.

requirements.title: HealthProvider trait — object safety and concurrency
requirements.text: The system shall provide a HealthProvider trait declaring health(&self) -> Health, matching go-DDS's dds.HealthProvider interface (Health() Health); the trait shall be object-safe (usable as Box<dyn HealthProvider> and Arc<dyn HealthProvider>) and Send + Sync, so a single provider instance may be shared across concurrent tokio tasks without the caller adding external synchronization.

requirements.title: HealthProvider wiring on every concrete Participant implementation
requirements.text: MockParticipant, ShmemParticipant, and RtpsUdpParticipant shall each implement HealthProvider, returning Health{status: Down, details: Some("{\"state\":\"closed\"}")} once the participant has been closed and Health{status: Ok, details: None} otherwise, matching go-DDS's mock.participant.Health, shmem.participant.Health, and rtps.participant.Health closed-state shape and details string byte-for-byte.
